{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What is an AI gateway?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"An AI gateway is a single API endpoint that sits between your application and multiple model providers. It centralizes credentials, routing, failover, and usage records, so your code talks to one API while the gateway manages many upstreams."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do I need an AI gateway if I only use one provider?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Usually not. A gateway earns its complexity when you use more than one provider, need automatic failover, or must track and cap spending across teams. Single-provider prototypes are fine calling the provider API directly."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How much does it cost to run an AI gateway?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Self-hosted open-source gateways are free to run on your own infrastructure; you pay only for the upstream model usage. Managed gateways typically charge a subscription or a markup on token spend, so compare that margin against the engineering time you save."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I migrate to an AI gateway without changing my code?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"If your application already uses the OpenAI SDK, migration usually means changing only the base URL and API key, because most gateways expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Anything that touches provider-specific features should be retested before production traffic moves."}}]}

{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Article","headline":"How to Reduce OpenAI API Costs in 2026: A Practical Playbook","description":"A practical playbook for cutting AI API spend with smart routing, token hygiene, caching, and per-key budgets — with verification steps for each tactic.","datePublished":"2026-11-09","dateModified":"2026-11-09","inLanguage":"en","mainEntityOfPage":"https://taodock.com/blog/reduce-openai-api-costs","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TaoDock"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"TaoDock","url":"https://taodock.com"}}

{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"How much can model routing save on AI API costs?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"It depends on your traffic mix. Teams that route trivial requests away from flagship models to cheaper tiers commonly see the largest single reduction, because per-token prices between tiers differ by an order of magnitude. Measure your own per-model spend first; the routing decision is only as good as the measurement behind it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does routing requests through a gateway add latency or cost?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A self-hosted gateway on the same network as your services adds a few milliseconds per request and no per-token markup. Managed gateways may charge a subscription or a token markup, so compare that fee against what the routing actually saves you."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is prompt caching and when does it help?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Prompt caching lets a provider reuse the processed prefix of a repeated prompt, charging a much lower rate for cached input tokens. It helps when many requests share a long identical prefix, such as a stable system prompt or the same reference document."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I stop one runaway script from blowing up my API bill?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Give every workload its own key with a hard budget, and let the gateway reject requests the moment the budget is spent. A retry loop without a budget is the most common cause of surprise five-figure invoices."}}]}

{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I create a TaoDock account?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Open the sign-up page, complete the required registration and verification steps, then sign in. Registration availability and methods may depend on the current deployment settings."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where do I create a TaoDock API key?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"After signing in, open the API keys area and create a key. Give each application or environment its own key so permissions, quota, rotation, and revocation can be managed independently."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I recover the full value of an API key later?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Treat the value shown at creation as a secret and store it securely. If a usable key value is lost or exposed, revoke it and create a replacement instead of sharing or logging it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What base URL should OpenAI-compatible clients use?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Most clients and SDKs should use https://taodock.com/v1. Some client presets, such as a host-oriented New API preset, may require https://taodock.com instead; follow the client-specific integration guide."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I find the correct model ID?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Use TaoDock's model page or call the /v1/models endpoint with the same API key. Copy the exact API ID returned to that key rather than guessing from a display name."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does TaoDock support every OpenAI API endpoint and parameter?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No universal compatibility claim applies to every endpoint, field, model, and upstream provider. Check the API guide and test the exact endpoint, model, and optional parameters your application uses."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why can my key see one model but not another?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Model visibility can depend on key restrictions, user group, configured channels, model availability, and deployment policy. Compare the key's permissions with the live model list."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the difference between account balance and key quota?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Account resources apply to the account, while a key can have a narrower usage limit. A request may be rejected by the key's limit even when the account still has available balance."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How are request charges determined?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Charges depend on the selected model, usage, pricing configuration, and applicable billing rules. Review the current pricing page and the request's usage record rather than relying on a permanent value in a tutorial."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What does a 401 error mean?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The API key is normally missing, invalid, disabled, expired, or sent to the wrong service. Recheck the Authorization value and base URL, and rotate the key if it may have been exposed."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What should I check for a 404 response?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Confirm the base URL and operation path, then verify the exact model ID. Avoid adding /v1 or a resource path twice when a client already appends it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why am I receiving a 429 or quota error?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Inspect whether the response represents rate limiting, account resources, or a key-level quota. Do not retry indefinitely; correct the limit or use bounded retries only for transient rate conditions."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why does streaming work on one network but not another?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"VPNs, reverse proxies, antivirus inspection, and corporate networks can buffer or terminate event streams. Compare a non-streaming request and a direct network before changing model or gateway settings."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why do tools, images, or files fail when text chat works?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Basic chat compatibility does not prove advanced feature support. Confirm the exact model and channel support the request format and capability, then test the smallest feature-specific request."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is it safe to put a TaoDock key in browser JavaScript?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. Code delivered to a public browser exposes the key to visitors. Keep the key in a trusted backend or controlled local client and have the browser call your authenticated server."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Should a team share one API key?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Prefer separate keys per application, environment, team, or user boundary. Separate credentials improve least privilege, usage attribution, rotation, incident containment, and revocation."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Which desktop and self-hosted clients can connect to TaoDock?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"OpenAI-compatible clients can often connect by changing their base URL, key, and model. TaoDock publishes guides for Cherry Studio, WorkBuddy, Open WebUI, AionUi, DeepChat, and SDK integrations."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What information should I include when troubleshooting a failed request?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Share the timestamp, endpoint, model, status, non-secret request identifier, client version, and a sanitized error. Never share API keys, Authorization headers, passwords, private prompts, or other credentials."}}]}
